messages.content: The summit coordinator finally answered. Presenter check-in is Thursday 3 to 6, Friday room access after 4:30, and Saturday lab teardown has to be done before the exhibit hall closes. Can we make the hotel call and book the flights if the fare is still there?

Yes. The practical split is clear now. Conference block: easiest for the Friday/Saturday movement; they can change the hold to a standard queen, coffee maker is confirmed, and I can attach a mini-fridge request, but the fridge is not guaranteed, the fitness room is small, and there is no pool or hot tub. Suite hotel: better room certainty with queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, workspace, and fitness access; still no pool or hot tub, and it adds a 12-14 minute walk or rideshare each teaching day. Flights: the 8:15 a.m. Thursday TPA-ATL-IND arriving 12:25 p.m. and the 1:55 p.m. Sunday IND-CLT-TPA arriving 6:32 p.m. are still available at $438.
That makes me lean conference block. I do not want to drag lab materials back and forth for a nicer room. Does the 12:25 arrival give enough room before presenter check-in?

It should. Land 12:25, rideshare to the hotel by about 1:10, leave bags with the bell desk if the room is not ready, then go to the presenter desk around 3:05. Plain caveat: if the room is not ready early, you may be organizing from the lobby for an hour or so. The block is still the more practical choice for the room changes.
Okay, use the block. Please switch it to the queen room and make the mini-fridge request obvious. I can deal with no pool or hot tub this time.

I can do that. Before I release the suite, the trade-off is final: the block wins on proximity, loses on recovery amenities, and only notes the mini-fridge request. The suite remains the safer in-room setup but costs you time on both teaching days. Do you want me to book air and update the block, then cancel the suite hold?
Yes. Book the Thursday 8:15 and the Sunday 1:55. If there is a window seat on the seat map, take it, but do not pay silly money just to get one.

Seat map check: free window seats are open on both Thursday legs and on the Charlotte-to-Tampa leg Sunday. The first Sunday leg only has aisle seats free right now; paid exit-row windows are $49, which I would skip unless you want that. Total remains $438 before standard bag fees.
Skip the paid exit row. Use the card on file and set a reminder to try for a window at check-in on that short Sunday leg.

Understood. I am booking the flights, updating the hotel block to the queen room, and keeping the mini-fridge note attached. One last point before I cancel the suite: without it, there is no guaranteed-fridge backup.
Cancel the suite anyway. Proximity matters more for this summit. Send me the confirmations and anything I still need to watch.

Booked and cleaned up. Flight confirmation INDAIR-6132: Thu Oct 10 TPA 8:15 a.m. to ATL 9:42, seat 14A; ATL 10:40 to IND 12:25, seat 15A. Sun Oct 13 IND 1:55 p.m. to CLT 3:38, seat 14C for now because no free window is open; reminder set to check again at T-24. CLT 5:05 to TPA 6:32, seat 18F. Airfare charged at $438. Hotel IND-BLOCK-7421 is updated to a standard queen for Oct 10-13 at the conference rate; coffee maker confirmed, mini-fridge request attached but not guaranteed, small fitness room, no pool or hot tub. Suite hold IND-SUITE-3186 is canceled. Watch items: early check-in is not guaranteed, Friday room access only after 4:30, and Saturday teardown has to finish before the exhibit hall closes.

Thursday plan: land 12:25, rideshare straight to the conference hotel, arrive around 1:10. If the room is not ready, bell desk the suitcase, keep the presenter folder and small kit with you, grab lunch, then check in at the presenter desk just after 3.
Good. How do I handle Friday if breakout-room access is only after 4:30?

Do not haul everything all day. Bring only what you need for the late-morning breakout. After the breakout, park the Saturday materials with presenter services or the bell desk until 4:30, then move them to the assigned prep area once room access opens.
And Saturday with that service corridor?

Use the service elevator instead of the public escalator. Drop the wheeled case in the marked corridor one level below before noon, bring only the active lab pieces up for the 1-4 session, then teardown 4:00-4:40 so everything is back downstairs before the exhibit hall closes.
What about Sunday checkout with the later flight?

Check out by 11:00, leave luggage with the bell desk, attend any final sessions until about 11:45 or noon, and leave the hotel by 12:10 for the 2:30 flight. Watch items: early check-in is not guaranteed, the mini-fridge is still a noted request rather than a promise, and you need the badge/access rule for the service corridor before Saturday.

messages.content: Switching gears from Indianapolis: the Atlanta-area pediatric mobility clinic wants me for Nov 7-8. Thursday is chart review plus a 5 p.m. room walkthrough, Friday is on-floor coaching. I need to know if this can be a one-night trip or if I should stay until Saturday.
I can compare it. Which part of Atlanta, and how firm is Friday end time? Also are you carrying only your own kit or anything bulky?

Decatur-ish. They want me in the clinic area by about 3:30 Thursday, walkthrough at 5. Friday demos are supposed to end 2:45, but the second team debrief could run long. Carry-on plus a small gait kit.

That makes the Thursday side easy and the Friday return the question. Direct TPA-ATL options I see: 9:35-11:07 gives lots of cushion; 11:10-12:42 is the best balance; 1:05-2:37 is too thin once you add bags and traffic. For returns, the 4:20 p.m. Friday is too close. A 6:45 p.m. direct works only if you are out by about 3:15. An 8:15 p.m. direct is the safer same-day return. Saturday has a 1:25 p.m. direct that makes the trip relaxed but adds a hotel night.
Do not rank this by cheapest. I need the option least likely to make Friday a sprint.

Then the practical order is: Saturday 1:25 p.m. return is safest; Friday 8:15 p.m. is the reasonable one-night plan; Friday 6:45 p.m. is only acceptable if the clinic gives a firm dismissal and helps with materials. I would ignore the 4:20.
What are the hotel choices?

Two useful ones. Host-adjacent hotel: 2-3 minute walk to the clinic, Google rating 3.9, standard queen, coffee maker listed, mini-fridge unclear/by request, and recovery amenities are not reliable in the listing. Suite property about ten minutes away: Google rating 4.4, queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, workspace, and fitness room confirmed; no pool or hot tub. The host hotel wins convenience; the suite wins reliability.
For one night I can live without the pool and hot tub, but I need coffee and a fridge. Is the ten-minute hotel really ten minutes?

Off-peak, yes: about 9-12 minutes. Friday morning I would budget 20, and late afternoon to the airport from the clinic is more like 45-65 depending on traffic. With just a carry-on and small kit, rideshare is simpler than renting unless they expect you to shuttle equipment.
I would rather not rent. But if the clinic assumes I am parking in their garage, we need to know that.

Agreed. Parking validation becomes a confirmation question, not a reason to rent now. Ask whether they expect you to drive, whether a staff or visitor garage pass is needed, and whether they validate if you do use a rental.
Between the hotels, I am leaning suite. The host-adjacent rating and fridge uncertainty bother me.

That is the cleaner pick. Caveat before booking later: the suite fixes the room basics but adds a rideshare for Thursday walkthrough and Friday morning. The host-adjacent hotel is the only option that lets you walk in and out, but it is the weaker room bet.
Now the return. I want to be home Friday if it is sane. I do not want to cut off questions at 2:45 just because I picked a bad flight.

Then use Friday 8:15 p.m. as Plan A, not the 6:45. If demos end at 2:45, you can debrief until around 3:45, leave by 4:15, and still have a buffer at ATL. If the debrief slips past 4:30, even 8:15 starts feeling long but still possible. Saturday 1:25 is the backup if they cannot promise an end.
Can we hold both returns?

Airline holds are limited on these fares. I can monitor both, but I would not purchase until the clinic answers. The risk is small fare movement; the bigger risk is buying Friday and then learning they expect you for a 4:30 wrap-up.
What exactly should I send them?

Send three questions: first, can the Friday coaching day and debrief be fully dismissed by 3:45, with someone empowered to cut Q&A if needed? Second, can your gait kit be stored securely after the Thursday walkthrough and during Friday lunch/debrief, and where do you retrieve it before leaving? Third, if a rental car is expected, what garage, validation code, or parking pass is provided; if not, where should rideshare pick up and drop off?
Good. Pencil Thursday 11:10, the suite hotel, and Friday 8:15 as Plan A. If they will not commit on dismissal or storage, Plan B is Saturday afternoon. Do not book until they answer.

Got it. Working plan, not booked: Thu Nov 7 TPA-ATL direct 11:10 a.m.-12:42 p.m.; rideshare to the Decatur clinic area with enough cushion for the 3:30 arrival and 5 p.m. walkthrough. Hotel target is the suite property for Nov 7-8: queen studio, coffee maker, mini-fridge, workspace, fitness room, no pool or hot tub. Plan A return is Fri Nov 8 ATL-TPA direct at 8:15 p.m. Plan B is extending the suite one more night and taking the Sat 1:25 p.m. direct. I will wait to book until the clinic confirms dismissal, kit storage, and parking/rideshare expectations; if fares jump before they answer, we will re-compare rather than force the Friday return.
